title: Quasi-coherence of arbitrary integer twists on Proj
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with an internal nonnegative grading $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$, denoted by $\mathcal A$; its pieces may be presented by any additive-subgroup class. For every integer $j$, the concrete twisting module sheaf $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Proj}(A)}(j)=\operatorname{twist}(\mathcal A,j)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] on $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Its sections are locally homogeneous fractions with numerator degree minus denominator degree $j$. No generation in degree one, no Noetherian hypothesis, and no positivity condition on $j$ is imposed.

proof.text: Extend the nonnegative grading to integers by zero in negative degrees and shift by j. Shifting reindexes an internal direct sum, and graded multiplication gives the module compatibility. Apply the graded-module sheaf construction to obtain its quasi-coherent associated sheaf. If the implementation requires AddSubgroup-valued pieces, transport along the identity graded ring maps between the two presentations: they give mutually inverse Proj maps and inverse maps on the homogeneous fractions and on their restrictions. The identity Proj maps send a prime to itself as an underlying ideal and are mutually inverse. At corresponding primes the maps on ordinary localizations are identity maps; the homogeneous membership conditions agree, so the pointwise section maps preserve addition and the structure-sheaf action and commute with restriction. This identifies the concrete twists along the scheme isomorphism, which preserves quasi-coherence.

For each positive homogeneous f, the single-twist fraction theorem identifies the concrete twist sections with the degree-zero fractions of the shifted ring. The fraction theorem gives additivity, bijectivity, the homogeneous-localization scalar law and the same y/f^m to a^m*y/g^(e*m) restriction formula as the associated sheaf whenever g^e=a*f.

The positive homogeneous standard opens form a basis. The compatible chart identifications therefore extend uniquely to an isomorphism of module sheaves. Transport quasi-coherence through this isomorphism. Empty Proj and empty charts are included, and negative j merely gives zero graded pieces where j+n<0.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 01MB, apply the associated graded-module construction to A(j); Definition 01MN and the concrete fraction identifications.
